verdict.detail: 3 underdogs under 5k followers, each with a past-week breakout: @halfdantimm 2,721 (92K views, ~150× his median), @nikolak47 2,845 (30.6K, ~7×), @harisahmad59 2,253 (31.6K). Every follower count, like and view count matches what its scripts returned. It says which were one-offs and which were already trending, and it lists the >5k accounts it excluded. Weak spots, all stated in the answer: only 3 posts, and one of Haris's two links is 8 days old.

answer:
I found three B2B founders under 5k followers with a clear breakout post this week, plus two borderline cases. That's a thin list. Google indexes few small-account posts, and most viral B2B SaaS posts this week came from accounts over 5k.

For each author I searched Google (`site:x.com`, past-week filter), then pulled their follower count and last ~40 posts through Reduck. "Baseline" is the median of those recent posts.

## Clear underdogs

**1. Halfdan Timm (@halfdantimm), 2,721 followers. One-off blow-up.**
- **What:** A text post. A SaaS salesperson wouldn't send a price without a meeting, so he built the product himself with AI in an hour, "while watching Toy Story 5 with the kids." He's co-founder of Obsidian, a marketing agency that has sold to private equity twice.
- **Numbers:** 278 likes, 128 bookmarks, 92K views (Sep 26).
- **Profile:** His posts usually get about 5 likes and 630 views, so this one got roughly 150× his normal reach. His only earlier breakout was an air-conditioning post in August (44K views). He wasn't trending before this.
- https://x.com/halfdantimm/status/2103923959481684000

**2. Nick Velkovski (@nikolak47), 2,845 followers. Already trending: repeat hits.**
- **What:** An X Article (a long-form post), shared as a bare link. Replies suggest it's his LinkedIn outreach workflow. He's CEO of HeyReach, which he describes as bootstrapped at $18M ARR.
- **Numbers:** 176 likes, 460 bookmarks, 30.6K views (Sep 22).
- **Profile:** His baseline is about 4.4K views, so this is roughly 7×. He's on a run of big posts:
  - Sep 8, bedroom-to-$17M-ARR story: 269K views
  - Aug 13, one customer to $17M ARR: 49K views
  
  So this is a small account with a proven formula (bootstrapped-ARR storytelling), not a lucky one-off.
- https://x.com/nikolak47/status/2102457147498140050

**3. Haris (@harisahmad59), 2,253 followers. Already trending: fast-growing account.**
- **What:** Short list posts, plus build-in-public updates about codehype.ai, a launch directory for startups.
  - Sep 24, "Claude $250 credits for FREE": 250 likes, 31.6K views
  - Sep 20, "High Authority Backlinks… Founders, save this list": 482 likes, 1,150 bookmarks, 35K views. This is 8 days old, just outside the window.
- **Profile:** By his own post on Sep 21, he went from 280 to 2K followers in a month. He posts several times a day, his median post already gets about 1.7K views, and he had several 10K+ view posts this week. This is steady growth, not a one-off.
- https://x.com/harisahmad59/status/2103040037281845431
- https://x.com/harisahmad59/status/2101599301957017701

## Borderline: under 5k followers but not strictly "B2B SaaS founders"

- **Max (@maxecc), 4,665 followers.** He's a B2B SaaS growth marketer (Google Ads) and an indie app builder. His Sep 25 post "I'm giving up on apps" says his app reached $3K MRR, then collapsed, and he's switching to running an agency. It got 275 likes and 38.7K views, against a baseline of about 600 views. This is his second spike in a month (an AI-blog SEO warning on Aug 30 got 28.5K views), so he may be starting to trend. https://x.com/maxecc/status/2103458858312081528
- **Rajath Gowda (@buildwithrajath), 1,457 followers.** His account was created in June 2026 and his bio says "~$10k MRR" for an AI SaaS. He posted 20+ times a day this week, with several 50K+ view hits. They're commentary on OpenAI and Anthropic, not B2B SaaS content. Example: https://x.com/buildwithrajath/status/2103383126378684679

## Excluded for having more than 5k followers
These had the biggest viral B2B SaaS posts this week:
- @vovudebosh ("Claude as your SDR" post, 6.3K+ likes): 30K followers
- @RobHoffman_: 14.8K
- @chhddavid: 18K
- @alexabelonix: 25.9K
- @coryalthoff ("SaaS is dead" rebuttal, 750+ likes): 5.9K, just over the cutoff

If you want a longer list, the next step is X's own search with a minimum-likes filter. Its results include each author's follower count, so it can find small accounts that Google misses.

Narrow queries return the same results in the same order across replays on one account/IP; very broad, high-volume queries may reorder between runs.

It’s about removing friction.

But most companies confuse the two. And it’s killing revenue.

Most founders think their product is truly self-serve.

In reality, only a few products in the world really are: Zoom, Calendly, Dropbox, Canva, Slack. Everyone else has friction hiding under the hood.

Even the best products come with innate complexity:
- Migrating contacts
- Setting up integrations
- Navigating compliance
- Rethinking workflows

And customers are not dumb... they’re just busy. For them, onboarding a new tool isn’t exciting. It’s another chore on an endless to-do list.

Here’s what I’ve seen across thousands of companies (and lived at Textline): when support owns free-trail or new customer onboarding, everything changes.

- Conversions often doubled (2–4x)
- Retention rose by 10%
- Time-to-value was cut in half
- Support tickets dropped (because customers were set up right the first time)
- Expectations were set early: bad fits disqualified themselves and good customers knew exactly what they were getting

Some call this Support-Led Growth (SLG).

It’s not about replacing PLG. It’s about plugging its biggest leak: activation.

And this isn’t just SaaS.

Any business with friction, logistics, trust, or setup complexity benefits from SLG. From SaaS to services, the principle is the same: a human in the loop accelerates value.

Here’s a thought matrix I use:
- High intent + high complexity > Concierge onboarding. Screen share, hand-holding, white-glove. Worth the investment because these users are serious but need help.
- High intent + low complexity > Guided self-serve with a human safety net. Think nudges, check-ins, optional setup calls.
- Low intent + high complexity > Disqualify fast. If they’re not committed, don’t burn cycles (this prevents churn before it happens).
- Low intent + low complexity > Pure self-serve. No human touch, minimal friction.

The best companies already practice SLG. They don’t just sell software. They make sure customers succeed on Day 1. That’s what builds retention, referrals, and reputation.

If you want PLG that actually scales, stop dreaming about “no-touch.” Invest in Support-Led Growth.

Your customers (and your revenue) will thank you.","created_at":"Thu Sep 25 15:59:36 +0000 2025","lang":"en","likes":4,"retweets":1,"replies":2,"quotes":0,"bookmarks":0,"views":190,"is_retweet":false,"is_quote":false,"source":"timeline"},{"id":"1970509952721789163","url":"https://x.com/mrajchan/status/1970509952721789163","text":"I was just at a pizza conference.

1. Treat CX like a product: CX in every PRD/roadmap/OKR. Architect the journey pre-sale (SLA, onboarding, handoffs) so nothing breaks post-close.

I found three B2B founders under 5k followers with a clear breakout post this week, plus two borderline cases. That's a thin list. Google indexes few small-account posts, and most viral B2B SaaS posts this week came from accounts over 5k.

For each author I searched Google (`site:x.com`, past-week filter), then pulled their follower count and last ~40 posts through Reduck. "Baseline" is the median of those recent posts.

## Clear underdogs

**1. Halfdan Timm (@halfdantimm), 2,721 followers. One-off blow-up.**
- **What:** A text post. A SaaS salesperson wouldn't send a price without a meeting, so he built the product himself with AI in an hour, "while watching Toy Story 5 with the kids." He's co-founder of Obsidian, a marketing agency that has sold to private equity twice.
- **Numbers:** 278 likes, 128 bookmarks, 92K views (Sep 26).
- **Profile:** His posts usually get about 5 likes and 630 views, so this one got roughly 150× his normal reach. His only earlier breakout was an air-conditioning post in August (44K views). He wasn't trending before this.
- https://x.com/halfdantimm/status/2103923959481684000

**2. Nick Velkovski (@nikolak47), 2,845 followers. Already trending: repeat hits.**
- **What:** An X Article (a long-form post), shared as a bare link. Replies suggest it's his LinkedIn outreach workflow. He's CEO of HeyReach, which he describes as bootstrapped at $18M ARR.
- **Numbers:** 176 likes, 460 bookmarks, 30.6K views (Sep 22).
- **Profile:** His baseline is about 4.4K views, so this is roughly 7×. He's on a run of big posts:
  - Sep 8, bedroom-to-$17M-ARR story: 269K views
  - Aug 13, one customer to $17M ARR: 49K views
  
  So this is a small account with a proven formula (bootstrapped-ARR storytelling), not a lucky one-off.
- https://x.com/nikolak47/status/2102457147498140050

**3. Haris (@harisahmad59), 2,253 followers. Already trending: fast-growing account.**
- **What:** Short list posts, plus build-in-public updates about codehype.ai, a launch directory for startups.
  - Sep 24, "Claude $250 credits for FREE": 250 likes, 31.6K views
  - Sep 20, "High Authority Backlinks… Founders, save this list": 482 likes, 1,150 bookmarks, 35K views. This is 8 days old, just outside the window.
- **Profile:** By his own post on Sep 21, he went from 280 to 2K followers in a month. He posts several times a day, his median post already gets about 1.7K views, and he had several 10K+ view posts this week. This is steady growth, not a one-off.
- https://x.com/harisahmad59/status/2103040037281845431
- https://x.com/harisahmad59/status/2101599301957017701

## Borderline: under 5k followers but not strictly "B2B SaaS founders"

- **Max (@maxecc), 4,665 followers.** He's a B2B SaaS growth marketer (Google Ads) and an indie app builder. His Sep 25 post "I'm giving up on apps" says his app reached $3K MRR, then collapsed, and he's switching to running an agency. It got 275 likes and 38.7K views, against a baseline of about 600 views. This is his second spike in a month (an AI-blog SEO warning on Aug 30 got 28.5K views), so he may be starting to trend. https://x.com/maxecc/status/2103458858312081528
- **Rajath Gowda (@buildwithrajath), 1,457 followers.** His account was created in June 2026 and his bio says "~$10k MRR" for an AI SaaS. He posted 20+ times a day this week, with several 50K+ view hits. They're commentary on OpenAI and Anthropic, not B2B SaaS content. Example: https://x.com/buildwithrajath/status/2103383126378684679

## Excluded for having more than 5k followers
These had the biggest viral B2B SaaS posts this week:
- @vovudebosh ("Claude as your SDR" post, 6.3K+ likes): 30K followers
- @RobHoffman_: 14.8K
- @chhddavid: 18K
- @alexabelonix: 25.9K
- @coryalthoff ("SaaS is dead" rebuttal, 750+ likes): 5.9K, just over the cutoff

If you want a longer list, the next step is X's own search with a minimum-likes filter. Its results include each author's follower count, so it can find small accounts that Google misses.
